To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incorporation of the HIV/AIDS identity into one's self occurs in three stages: (a) diagnosis, (b) a postdiagnosis point of turning, and (c) integration.

the HIV identity is incorporated into the self through a process that includes three steps: (a) diagnosis; (b) a turning point, which is a time when the individual realizes that the HIV identity has become part of the self; and (c) integration, when the HIV identity is fully incorporated into the self and becomes an integral part of the self-concept.
people who were diagnosed after the advent of antiretroviral therapy (ART) in 1996 experienced a three-step process of incorporating the HIV identity into the self.

people with HIV/AIDS are able to incorporate their HIV/AIDS identity and live full lives.

people who have been living with HIV for many years have been able to incorporate the HIV identity into the self.
the HIV/AIDS identity is a normal part of the human experience, and that it can be incorporated into the self without causing undue harm to one's sense of self.
